title: A2 final test
intro: Thirty questions from the whole of A2; each attempt draws 20. You need 80% to pass. You see the explanations at the end.

items.prompt: Wczoraj Marek i Ola ___ w teatrze.
items.explanation: A group with at least one man takes the -li form: Marek i Ola byli.
optionNotes: -ły is for groups without men: Ola i Kasia były.
Był is one man; the subject here is two people.
Byliśmy means "we were"; the subject is Marek and Ola, so "they".

items.explanation: Móc has ó only in mógł (he could). Every other past form has o: mogła, mogłem, mogli.

items.prompt: Wczoraj w końcu ___ ten raport. (A man speaking: I finally finished writing it.)
items.explanation: One finished action with a result takes the perfective, and w końcu (finally) signals it: napisałem.
optionNotes: Pisałem is the imperfective: it says you were writing, not that the report is done.
Piszę is the present; wczoraj needs the past.
Będę pisać is the future; wczoraj needs the past.

items.prompt: Kiedy byłam mała, codziennie ___ z babcią. (When I was little, I cooked with my grandma every day.)
items.explanation: A repeated action in the past takes the imperfective, and codziennie (every day) signals it: gotowałam.
optionNotes: Ugotowałam is the perfective: one finished meal, not a habit.
Gotuję is the present; the story is in the past.
Ugotuję is the perfective future: "I will cook".

items.prompt: Wieczorem ___ do ciebie e-mail. (napisać, I)
items.explanation: Napisać is perfective, so its present-looking form means the future, with no będę: napiszę.

items.prompt: Od roku ___ do pracy rowerem. (a habit)
items.explanation: A regular trip by vehicle takes jeździć: jeżdżę. Jechać is for one trip in one direction.
optionNotes: Jadę is one trip now, not a habit.
Pojadę is one trip in the future.
Jechałem is the past of one trip ("I was riding"); od roku describes a habit that goes on now.

items.explanation: Bać się always has się and takes the genitive: psów. Się never starts the sentence.

items.prompt: A sign in a museum says that taking photos is not allowed. Which sentence says this?
items.explanation: Nie wolno means "you mustn't": a ban. Because of nie, the object takes the genitive: zdjęć (compare Wolno robić zdjęcia).
optionNotes: Nie musisz means "you don't have to", not "you mustn't".
Warto means "it's worth it": the opposite of a ban.
Trzeba means "you have to".

items.prompt: At the reception desk you politely ask a man you don't know to wait a moment. You say:
items.explanation: To a stranger use proszę + infinitive: Proszę chwilę poczekać.
optionNotes: Poczekaj is the ty command: for friends, family and children.
After proszę to a stranger use the infinitive, not the ty form.
Poczekasz is the future ("you'll wait"), not a polite request, and it uses ty, which is too familiar for a stranger.

items.prompt: Ania i Paweł są bardzo ___.
items.explanation: A group with a man takes the masculine personal plural, and ł changes to l: mili.
optionNotes: Miłe is for groups without men: Ania i Ola są miłe.
Miła is one woman.
Miły is one man; są needs a plural.

items.context: At the weekend I visit my parents.
items.explanation: Rodzice is masculine personal, so the accusative plural takes -ów, and "my" takes moich: moich rodziców.

items.prompt: Na koncercie było dużo ___.
items.explanation: After dużo the noun takes the genitive plural; ludzie is irregular: ludzi.
optionNotes: Ludzie is the nominative plural; dużo needs the genitive.
Ludźmi is the instrumental: z ludźmi.
Osoby is the nominative plural; the genitive would be osób.

items.prompt: Kupiłam ___ nowy telefon. (I bought my brother a new phone.)
items.explanation: The person who gets something takes the dative; brat is on the short list with -u: bratu.
optionNotes: Brata is the accusative or genitive; the receiver needs the dative.
Bratem is the instrumental: z bratem (with my brother).
Do means "to a place"; the receiver takes the dative with no preposition.

items.source: Moi rodzice uczą w szkole. To nauczyciele.
items.explanation: A job after a form of być takes the instrumental, in the plural too: -ami. Nauczyciele → nauczycielami.

items.prompt: Po ___ idę na siłownię. (praca)
items.explanation: Po meaning "after" takes the locative; praca ends in -ca, so the locative is -y: po pracy.

items.prompt: Ola ma dwadzieścia dwa ___.
items.explanation: From 22 on the last digit decides: 2, 3, 4 take the 2–4 form, lata.
optionNotes: Lat is the 5+ form: dwadzieścia pięć lat.
Roku is the genitive singular, not used for counting years.
Rok is the form after jeden (one).

items.prompt: Znasz Tomka? — Tak, znam ___ dobrze.
items.explanation: The object needs the accusative; with no stress and no preposition use the short form go.
optionNotes: On is the nominative, the subject form.
Niego is used after a preposition: dla niego, do niego.
Mu is the dative (to him); znać takes the accusative.

items.prompt: Pociąg jest ___ niż autobus.
items.explanation: A short adjective takes -szy for "-er": szybki → szybszy. Niż means "than".
optionNotes: Bardziej is for long adjectives; szybki has its own form, so bardziej szybki is not the normal way to say it.
Szybciej is the adverb (faster, of an action); after jest describing the train you need the adjective.
Najszybszy means "the fastest"; niż compares two things.

items.explanation: Every negative word needs nie before the verb: Nikt nie dzwonił. Nikt is masculine, so the verb ends in -ł.

items.prompt: Ja piję kawę, ___ Ola pije herbatę.
items.explanation: A contrast between two people takes a, with a comma before it.
optionNotes: I adds similar things and takes no comma; a contrast needs a.
Albo means "or" (a choice); here both people drink something.
Czy is "or" in a question.

items.prompt: A friend asks how your weekend was. It was great. You say:
items.explanation: Polish says "it was great" with było and no subject: Było super!
optionNotes: Miałem dobry czas is a word-for-word copy of "I had a good time"; Polish does not say it.
Byłem dobrze is not Polish: with a person as the subject, być takes an adjective (Byłem zadowolony). The adverb goes with impersonal było: Było dobrze, Było super.
Jestem super is the present and means "I'm great", not that the weekend was.

items.prompt: ___ jest twój nowy sąsiad? — Bardzo miły.
items.explanation: "What … like?" is jaki, and it agrees with the noun: sąsiad is masculine, so jaki.
optionNotes: Jak asks "how"; for "what is he like" use jaki.
Co asks "what" (a thing), not what someone is like.
Jaka is the feminine form: Jaka jest twoja nowa sąsiadka?

items.prompt: A woman you don't know asks you the way. Tell her to go straight on.
items.explanation: Directions to a stranger: proszę + infinitive, Proszę iść prosto.
optionNotes: After proszę use the infinitive, not the present form idzie.
Idziesz prosto is a statement ("you're going straight") and uses ty.
Idź is the ty command, for friends; to a stranger use proszę + infinitive.

items.prompt: A friend invites you to the cinema on Saturday, but you're working. Which answer is polite?
items.explanation: Decline with niestety and a short reason after bo; a bare nie sounds cold.
optionNotes: A bare nie sounds cold; add a reason.
Nie chcę kina is not natural Polish, and it sounds rude.
Ochota takes na + accusative (ochotę na kino), and saying you don't feel like it is not a polite reason.

items.prompt: W pokoju nie ___ ogrzewanie. (The heating in my room doesn't work.)
items.explanation: For machines and devices "work" is działać, not pracować: Nie działa ogrzewanie. In everyday speech you will also hear nie chodzi.

items.prompt: You have a headache. You tell the doctor:
items.explanation: Polish says "the head hurts me": the head is the subject, the person is in the accusative: Boli mnie głowa.
optionNotes: A word-for-word copy of English: grammatical, but Polish doesn't say it. Polish puts the person in the accusative: boli mnie.
Bolą is plural; głowa is one thing, so boli.
Głowa is the subject, so it stays in the nominative.

items.prompt: Na następnym przystanku ___. (I'm getting off at the next stop.)
items.explanation: Getting off a bus or train is wysiadać / wysiąść: wysiadam.
optionNotes: Wsiadam means "I'm getting on".
Przesiadam się means "I'm changing" to another bus or train.
Odjeżdżam means "I'm leaving, driving off".

items.prompt: Match the English words with their Polish equivalents.
items.explanation: Trousers = spodnie (plural only), coat = płaszcz, fitting room = przymierzalnia, receipt = paragon.

items.prompt: Jaka jest dziś pogoda? — ___ deszcz.
items.explanation: Rain and snow "fall" in Polish: Pada deszcz (it's raining).
optionNotes: Jest deszcz is a word-for-word guess; Polish says the rain falls: pada.
Mieć does not describe the weather.
Robić does not describe the weather.

items.prompt: W sobotę gram z synem ___ piłkę.
items.explanation: Games and sports take grać w + accusative: gram w piłkę.
optionNotes: Grać na is for instruments: gram na gitarze.
Do means "to a place"; it is not used with grać.
Z means "with": z synem is already in the sentence.
